title: Your smartwatch might be giving your workouts more credit than they deserve
summary: Your body fat percentage could be throwing off your smartwatch's calorie counter.
body: TL;DR A new study finds that popular smartwatches from Apple, Samsung, Garmin, and Fitbit substantially miscalculate calories burned during exercise. The higher your body fat percentage, the less accurate your smartwatch’s calorie estimates may be, with errors reaching 100% or more. Researchers recommend treating smartwatch calorie counts as rough estimates, especially if you rely on them to manage your weight. If you own a smartwatch , you know the satisfaction that comes after finishing a strenuous workout, glancing at your wrist, and seeing just how many calories you’ve burned. If your aim is to be in a calorie deficit and lose weight, that figure on the watch holds a lot of importance. However, a new study suggests that your smartwatch might not be giving you accurate readings, especially if you have a higher body fat percentage . Smartwatches have become increasingly common , not just because of their health and fitness tracking prowess, but also because of their convenience. Specifically, the conversation turned on Ja Rule’s Oct. 2004 single “New York,” which featured Joe and Jadakiss, as well as lines from Ja that 50 took as a sneak diss. Lil’ Kim [who briefly dated Storch at the time], she’ll tell you. I had Lil Kim dancing like this [shakes his shoulders], like, ‘Move ya body like a snake, mama,’ I had her doing that to ‘Candy Shop.'” Joe said producer Storch called him “20, 30 times…

title: Google gets another $460 million fine for misusing user data
summary: The Irish data privacy regulator found Google guilty misusing users' location history and web activity.
body: Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority TL;DR Google has been fined €403 million ($462 million) for misusing European users’ location history and web browsing activity. The Irish DPC, acting on behalf of the EU, said Google stores users’ location data, violating the GDPR. It also said the data could have been used for targeted advertising or to influence users’ decisions. Google hasn’t had a particularly rewarding 2026, and its legal troubles don’t seem to end. In July 2026, the European Court of Justice held that Google had violated its dominant position by pushing its own services and reserved its previous judgment in the landmark antitrust case, along with a penalty of $4.67 billion . Later that month, the European Commission fined Google close to $1 billion for allegedly violating the Digital Markets Act (DMA). While this was followed by some relief from previously suggested extreme measures in the United States vs. Google lawsuit regarding its monopoly in digital ads, Google has now been hit with another fine of close to half a billion dollars. Google has now been fined €403 million ($462 million) by the Irish data privacy watchdog Data Protection Commission (DPC) for alleged…

title: Forgot your phone PIN? Google could look to the past to save you from a factory reset
summary: You could soon use your Google account credentials to recover your locked device, just like you could back in the day.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Android 17 QPR2 Beta 5 includes code for a “Unlock with Google Account” feature, which would let users recover locked-out phones without performing a factory reset. Google previously allowed pattern unlock resets using Google account credentials until Android 4.4, but later removed the feature, forcing everyone locked out of their phone to factory reset. The unreleased feature appears to be optional, which would balance the needs of everyday consumers and security-conscious users. Google released Android 17 QPR2 Beta 5 last week, and we are digging into the release to see what the company has in store for us. We’ve now found clues of a new feature in the works that could soon let you unlock your Android phone with your linked Google account credentials if you ever forget your PIN or password, which could finally save users from the nuclear option of a factory reset when they are locked out of their devices. title: T-Mobile customers could soon experience much better 5G even outside the US

body: TL;DR T-Mobile and Jio have achieved the world’s first 5G standalone roaming connection. It could enable seamless transfers between the two carriers’ networks when roaming. 5G standalone roaming could also enable better enterprise and AI applications. T-Mobile was one of the first carriers to roll out a standalone 5G network and has steadily improved its 5G speeds and availability. In fact, some reports say it’s one of the best-performing US carriers . While T-Mobile may have made some controversial decisions regarding its legacy plans, the Un-carrier now proudly boasts yet another achievement. T-Mobile has announced that it has achieved the world’s first 5G standalone roaming connection in partnership with Indian carrier Jio. 5G standalone (SA) networks use a dedicated 5G architecture end-to-end and are usually faster and have lower latency than 5G non-standalone (NSA) networks, which rely on 4G core infrastructure.

title: The smart glasses market has more than doubled in the last year, with Meta dominating
summary: Smart glasses had a huge first half of 2026, with Meta way out in front and display-less models accounting for 96%.
body: Credit: Chase Bernath / Android Authority TL;DR Global AI glasses shipments jumped 263% year over year in H1 2026, according to Counterpoint Research. Display-less models accounted for 96% of shipments, with Meta holding a dominant 94% share of that segment. Shipments of AR glasses surged 449% year over year, albeit from a low base. Smart glasses might still feel like a niche category of tech, but they seem to be selling at a much faster clip than they were a year ago. Global AI glasses shipments jumped 263% year over year in the first half of 2026, and the vast majority weren’t AR specs. Counterpoint Research’s latest Intelligent Eyewear Market Tracker attributes most of that growth to the cheaper, more mature display-less category, which includes products such as the Ray-Ban Meta AI Glasses. Shipments in this segment rose 258% year over year and 22% compared with the second half of 2025.

title: More Android phones in US, EU could finally get huge batteries, thanks to Apple
summary: Apple just showed Android OEMs how to get around battery capacity regulations.
body: Credit: Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority TL;DR Apple has revealed the Prepare to Ship feature for the iPhone 18 Pro Max, and we hope Android OEMs copy this option. This feature caps the iPhone’s battery capacity during transport, allowing the iPhone 18 Pro Max to meet transport requirements in many countries. The cap is removed once the phone is activated, allowing for higher battery capacities in Europe, the US, and other markets. Smartphone batteries have grown exponentially in the last few years, with 6,000mAh, 7,000mAh, and even 10,000mAh batteries on the market. Unfortunately, transport regulations in many markets place a cap on the size of an individual battery cell. This forces smartphone makers to adopt dual-cell battery designs or use smaller batteries, but Apple has revealed a nifty solution with the iPhone 18 Pro Max. Europe, the US, and international transport networks have a 20Wh cap on a small single-cell battery . That’s roughly equivalent to a maximum capacity of 5,300mAh. However, the iPhone 18 Pro Max has a 5,391mAh battery in global models. So how did Apple get around this restriction?

body: I’ve tested dozens of wireless chargers and desk setups over the years, and most of them suffer from the same problem. They all try to shoehorn everything into a single hub. There’s little, if any, flexibility in placement, choice of charging options, or future upgradeability. Moreover, as a design enthusiast, I care a lot about how a particular piece of tech looks in my space, and most chargers just aren’t very pretty to look at. But looks are subjective. Anyway, the fact is that most charging stations expect you to conform to a fixed layout for your phone, earbuds, and smartwatch . That’s fine for a functional product, but for one, the fixed layout has never really suited how I use my phone. Want to rearrange things? Tough luck.

title: This simple Duolingo trick brings back hearts and gets rid of the annoying ads

body: Credit: Matt Horne / Android Authority Even as one of the last remaining Duolingo holdouts on the team, I can see how much worse Duolingo has become in recent years. The once-motivating gamification certainly appears to have been kicked up a few notches, and it’s the free users who’ve had it much worse. On the free plan, you’re bombarded with adverts for Super Duolingo and third-party games that you can’t skip for several seconds. Even worse, the heart system that allowed you to keep practicing until you made five mistakes was replaced by an energy bar that runs down even if you’re nailing the answers. That’s why I was excited to learn about a very simple trick that returns you to a simpler version of Duolingo — one with the hearts system, no ads at all, fewer clicks between lessons, and less gamification.
